primaryText: A: Who does Bo admire? B: Bo?
translation: A: Who does Bo admire? B: Bo?
comment: Reading 1 (short answer): 'Does Bo admire Bo?'; reading 2 (clausal confirmation): 'Are you asking who Bo (of all people) admires?'; reading 2 (intended content): 'Who do you mean Bo?'. Against Equal Access to Context: only the addressee has the two clarification readings.

primaryText: A: Who does Bo admire? Bo?
translation: A: Who does Bo admire? Bo?
comment: Reading 1 (short answer): 'Does Bo admire Bo?'; reading 2 (self-correction): 'Did I say Bo?'. Only the original speaker has the self-correction reading.

primaryText: A: Which members of this audience own a parakeet? Why?
discourseSegments: A: Which members of this audience own a parakeet?
translation: A: Which members of this audience own a parakeet? Why?
comment: The Turn-Taking Puzzle: 'Why?' = 'Why own a parakeet?'; the resolution of bare 'why' depends on who holds the turn.

primaryText: A: Which members of this audience own a parakeet? B: Why?
discourseSegments: A: Which members of this audience own a parakeet?
translation: A: Which members of this audience own a parakeet? B: Why?
comment: 'Why?' = 'Why are you asking which members of this audience own a parakeet?'; the reading available to B is unavailable to A in (23a), and vice versa.

primaryText: A: Which members of this audience own a parakeet? Why am I asking this question?
discourseSegments: A: Which members of this audience own a parakeet?
A: Why am I asking this question?
translation: A: Which members of this audience own a parakeet? Why am I asking this question?
comment: The resolution unavailable to A with bare 'Why?' is a coherent follow-up when expressed non-elliptically, so the (23a)/(23b) asymmetry is not a matter of coherence or plausibility.

primaryText: A: Hi. B: Hi. A: Who's coming tomorrow? B: Several colleagues of mine (are coming). A: I see. B: Mike (is coming) too.
discourseSegments: B: Several colleagues of mine (are coming).
translation: A: Hi. B: Hi. A: Who's coming tomorrow? B: Several colleagues of mine (are coming). A: I see. B: Mike (is coming) too.
comment: Traced in (55)–(63) through greeting, counter-greeting, Free Speech, Ask QUD-incrementation, QSPEC, Assert QUD-incrementation, Accept and Fact update/QUD-downdate.

primaryText: A: Who should we invite for tomorrow? B: Who will agree to come? A: Helen and Jelle and Fran and maybe Sunil. B: (a) I see. (b) So, Jelle I think. A: OK.
discourseSegments: A: Who should we invite for tomorrow?
B: Who will agree to come?
A: Helen and Jelle and Fran and maybe Sunil.
B: (a) I see. (b) So, Jelle I think.
translation: A: Who should we invite for tomorrow? B: Who will agree to come? A: Helen and Jelle and Fran and maybe Sunil. B: (a) I see. (b) So, Jelle I think. A: OK.
comment: Traced in (66): B's question influences A's; A's answer resolves B's question and is accepted, leaving A's question QUD-maximal.

primaryText: A: (a) Bo is now in Essen, (b) is he? B: Yes.
discourseSegments: A: (a) Bo is now in Essen, (b) is he?
translation: A: (a) Bo is now in Essen, (b) is he? B: Yes.
comment: Traced in (68): the asserter checks their own assertion; the addressee confirms.

primaryText: A: (1a) Who will Max be inviting? (1b) When will these guests be arriving? B: Mary and Bill. A: Aha. B: Tomorrow or the day after most likely.
discourseSegments: A: (1a) Who will Max be inviting? (1b) When will these guests be arriving?
B: Tomorrow or the day after most likely.
translation: A: (1a) Who will Max be inviting? (1b) When will these guests be arriving? B: Mary and Bill. A: Aha. B: Tomorrow or the day after most likely.
comment: Traced in (79): successive questions by one speaker; the second does not influence the first, which stays QUD-maximal and is answered first.

primaryText: A: Hi. B: I'm off. A: OK. B: Bye.
translation: A: Hi. B: I'm off. A: OK. B: Bye.
comment: B takes the genre to be CasualChat, whose anticipated issues are how A is and how B is; 'I'm off' is an initiating move about the latter.

primaryText: A: Is George here? B: Is WHO here? A: George Sand. B: Ah, no.
translation: A: Is George here? B: Is WHO here? A: George Sand. B: Ah, no.
context: B is unsure about the intended reference of 'George'.
comment: B initiates clarification by Parameter Focussing; the gameboards after the second utterance are given in Ch. 6 (91) and differ in QUD and PENDING.

primaryText: A: Did Bo leave? B: Bo? A: Your cousin.
translation: A: Did Bo leave? B: Bo? A: Your cousin.
comment: Other-initiated repair: a clarification request across utterances.

primaryText: A: [Did Bo + {I mean} my cousin] leave?
translation: A: Did Bo, I mean my cousin, leave?
comment: Self-initiated mid-utterance repair, the within-utterance analogue of (24a). Switchboard-style annotation: '+' marks the moment of interruption, '{}' the editing term.
